standard.title: Investigate composers and performers across contexts
standard.description: investigate the ways that composers and/or performers use the elements of music and/or compositional devices in music composed across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore ways that the elements of music are combined in music across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts (AC9AMU6E01). They have explored rather than investigated — they have not yet analysed how elements and devices are used with the specific purpose of informing their own performance or composition decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how composers and/or performers use elements of music and compositional devices in music across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts, using this investigation to describe stylistic features and inform their own practice.

nodes.label: Accessing and analysing music across contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can access and analyse music from a range of cultural, historical or contextual sources, identifying how elements of music are manipulated and how compositional devices are used
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse at least one piece of music from a specified context (culture, time or place); identify at least two ways elements of music are manipulated or compositional devices are used
nodes.typical_width: Analyse music across multiple contexts; identify stylistic characteristics through listening; connect analytical observations to the cultural, historical or contextual background
wider: Access multiple live or recorded performances and analyse how performers interpret the same stylistic conventions differently — identify which elements are fixed by style and which are open to interpretive choice

Analyse how elements of music are manipulated in music composed with social intent (protest songs, nationalistic music, music about identity or belonging) — connect specific musical choices to the intended message

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate experience with a range of musical contexts before they can identify what is style-specific versus universal. Analysis of multiple pieces — across cultures, times and places — builds the comparative reference base that stylistic description depends on.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The social intent direction (protest songs, nationalistic music, identity and belonging) offers genuinely rich analytical territory — students connect musical choices to real-world communicative purposes, developing a critical listening lens that goes meaningfully beyond identifying stylistic features.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two ways elements of music are manipulated or devices are used in a piece
Connects the analysis to the cultural, historical or contextual background

nodes.label: Describing stylistic features of genres and styles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the stylistic features of a musical style or genre using music terminology, based on analytical listening
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two stylistic features of one genre or style using music terminology; the description is specific enough to distinguish this style from others
nodes.typical_width: Describe the stylistic features of multiple genres or styles; use terminology consistently and accurately; identify what makes each style distinctive
wider: Compare the stylistic features of two genres that share historical roots (e.g. blues and rock, folk and country, Western classical and film scores) — identify what was inherited and what diverged

Research the social, cultural and historical developments that shaped a specific style or tradition (e.g. 32-bar song form, chamber music, singer-songwriter) — explain how these developments are reflected in the music's stylistic features

response_modes.reason: Students frequently describe stylistic features in generic terms ('it sounds old-fashioned', 'it has a strong beat') that don't distinguish between styles. Encountering multiple styles and practising comparative description — what this style does that others don't — builds the specificity that useful stylistic description requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The historical roots/divergence direction is genuinely rich — connecting stylistic features to cultural and historical development gives students an analytical framework that extends their understanding well beyond checklist-style feature identification.
success_criteria: Describes at least two stylistic features of a genre or style using music terminology
The description is specific enough to distinguish the style from at least one other

nodes.label: Analysing performer interpretation of composer intentions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how performers interpret composers' intentions, identifying specific choices about tempo, instrumentation, feel or articulation and evaluating their effect
nodes.minimum_width: Use a recording and available score, chart or other information (interview, review) to identify at least one way a performer has interpreted a composer's intention; explain the effect of that interpretive choice
nodes.typical_width: Analyse multiple interpretive choices (tempo, instrumentation, feel, articulation) in a performance; evaluate how the choices relate to the composer's apparent intentions
wider: Compare two recordings of the same work to identify where interpretive choices diverge — evaluate which interpretation is more aligned with the composer's apparent intentions and justify the judgement
Access an interview or review alongside a recording and score to triangulate performer intentions with composer intentions — identify where they align and where they diverge

response_modes.reason: Analysing interpretation requires students to hold two perspectives simultaneously — composer intention and performer choice — and reason about the relationship between them. Scaffolding this reasoning (what does the score/chart show → what did the performer do → how do these relate) prevents students from simply describing what they hear without engaging the interpretive layer.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one interpretive choice made by a performer
Explains how the choice relates to the composer's apparent or documented intentions

nodes.label: Using investigation to inform own practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use their investigation of composers' and performers' use of elements and devices to inform specific choices in their own performance or composition
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one choice in their own performance or composition that was informed by their investigation; explain the connection
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate multiple connections between investigative findings and practice decisions; explain how understanding a style or tradition informed how they approached their own work in that style
wider: Research a style or tradition in depth, then use that research to develop a set of rehearsal or composition aims — evaluate how well the resulting work reflects the stylistic understanding gained
Incorporate findings from research into social, cultural and historical developments into a performance or composition — reflect on how the research changed or deepened their musical choices

response_modes.reason: This node connects investigation (analysis, description, interpretation) to practice (composing, performing). The integration of analytical understanding into creative and technical decision-making is the learning — students discover that research about music informs what they do as musicians.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one practice decision informed by investigation
Can explain the connection between what they found and what they decided
